content.text:
NaYb(Pd3O4)2 (mp-1209950) is the only phase I can find in this pattern.

- **Peak match:** The observed peaks sit at about 15.3, 26.7, 30.9, 34.7, 38.1 and 44.25° two-theta. These are the positions expected for its primitive cubic cell (a ≈ 5.78 Å). The relative intensities also match: the 34.7° peak is the strongest at 100, and 38.1° comes in at about 68 observed against 65 simulated.
- **Fit quality:** The single-phase fit gave an R-factor of 0.72 at zero strain. That is high, but the residual is mostly paired positive and negative swings at each peak, and I read those as the simulated peaks being broader than the observed ones, not as missing peaks.
- **Second phase:** Apart from those swings the residual is flat, with no structured peaks. The only small leftover feature is near 74–75°, and the simulated pattern itself has a weak peak there.
- **Other candidates:** Sr2CrReO6 and Ba2SmMnO6 each gave an R-factor of about 1.0 and left almost the whole pattern unexplained. I didn't fit the other six candidates. I also didn't run a two-phase fit, so ruling out a second phase rests only on the flat residual.

{"present": ["mp-1209950"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "Every observed peak matches the primitive cubic NaYb(Pd3O4)2 cell (a≈5.78 Å) in position and relative intensity, and apart from peak-width mismatch the residual shows no second phase."}
